newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends easier vs forward dlr,spot steady.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends easier vs forward dlr,spot steady.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed weaker on Tuesday against the forward dollar but the central bank again intervened to stop the currency strengthening on the spot market, dealers said.
The six month annualised premium closed the day at 5.66 percent compared to the previous close of 5.54 percent.
The spot rupee closed at 35.710/7150 to the dollar compared to 35.705/710 opening and Monday's close of 35.6900/700, dealers said.
The RBI bought spot dollars from 35.71 to 35.72 levels, dealers said.
The rupee traded in a range of 35.7025 to 35.7225 on Tuesday.

The forward market continued to be volatile following Reserve Bank of India deputy governor Y.V. Reddy's comment on Friday that the rupee was overvalued based on its real effective exchange rate performance.
"Stop loss sales are triggered at every rise," said a bank dealer. "It all started with RBI's (Reserve Bank of India) comments about rupee's overvaluation at Goa."
Forward premiums opened up, moved higher and despite a late correction closed above Monday's closing levels, dealers said.
July dollars touched a high of 2.07 rupees on Tuesday before closing the day at 1.95/1.98 rupees, dealers said.
July dollars closed 1.90/1.93 rupees on Monday.
Dealers said some firms were covering up to January.
They said a leading petrochemicals and textiles firm, which began covering one year forwards on Monday, was again in the market on Tuesday.
But other dealers said the rise in premiums were not entirely corporate-driven.
"I haven't seen any major corporate covering this week," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Many banks are cutting their huge received positions after (RBI deputy governor) Reddy's speech at Goa," a dealer said.
Dealers said several banks, which normally keep their foreign currency deposits in dollars have begun swapping them into rupees after Reddy's comments.
